P1.why: Source P1: slab/corner over roofs, belay at two-bolt anchor.
P1.text: Stance is at the top of the slabby corner, above the small roofs, on a two-bolt anchor.

P2.why: Source P2: belay in a stem box at two offset bolts.
P2.text: The station sits inside a stemming box at the end of the undercling traverse, on two bolts set offset from each other.

P4.why: Source P4: belay on a ledge at a two-bolt anchor; 'above the hard bolted section' unstated, removed.
P4.text: Belay on a ledge at the top of the pitch, on a two-bolt anchor.

P6.why: Source P6: single bolt backed up with a cam; pitch ends on the west ridge.
P6.text: The station is a lone bolt at the top of the headwall, backed up with a small cam, on the West Ridge.

1.why: MP P1: belay near small rotting tree (page says below it); made neutral.
1.text: Belay by a small rotting tree once the bouldery start gives way to easier ground.

3.why: MP P3: short slab to Launch Ledge; move belay ~30 ft left before P4.
3.text: Finish on Launch Ledge above the dihedral and short slab, then shift the belay roughly thirty feet left before the Scoop pitch.

4.why: MP P4: finishes with hand crack to a belay ledge.
4.text: The station is a ledge at the top of the hand-crack finish above the giant scooped corner.

5.why: MP P5: move out and left of the roof to a belay ledge.
5.text: Belay on a ledge reached by moving out and left around the small roof.

6.why: MP P6: belay is a tree on the final ledge.
6.text: The last technical stance is a ledge with a tree for the anchor.

P1.why: Source P1: corner, belay at ledge with two bolts.
P1.text: Belay from a ledge at the top of the corner, anchored on two bolts.

P2.why: Source P2: traverse left, thin corner, ledge with two-bolt belay; 'layback' not in source, removed.
P2.text: The station is a ledge after the leftward traverse and corner, with a two-bolt anchor.

P3.why: Source P3: Sky Lounge, a ledge with two bolts; 'roomy' unstated, removed.
P3.text: Stance is the Sky Lounge, a ledge at the top of the corner, on two bolts.

P4.why: Source P4: two-bolt anchor in an alcove, last rappel point.
P4.text: Belay in an alcove at the top of the crux pitch, on a two-bolt anchor that is the last point from which you can rappel.

P5.why: Source P5: gear belay in sandy alcove.
P5.text: Build the anchor from gear in a sandy alcove at the end of the crack.

2.why: Both sources P2: huge ledge; one says right side of the crest; 'beside the crest' vague.
2.text: Belay on a very large ledge at the top of the hand crack, on the right side of the crest.

3.why: MP P3: obvious good ledge after roofy black-band section.
3.text: The station is a good ledge above the roof pulls through the black band.

4.why: MP P4: sloping ledge with fixed pin and gear seam.
4.text: Stop on a sloping ledge, using a fixed pin plus gear in a seam.

6.why: MP P6: exit to an easy slab belay.
6.text: Stance is on an easy slab at the top of the pitch.

1.why: Both sources P1: bolts/anchors on a ledge.
1.text: The station is a ledge at the top of the narrowing crack, equipped with bolts.

2.why: P2: ledge with bolts (3-bolt anchor in one source) after bulge.
2.text: Belay on a ledge above the bulge, with a three-bolt anchor.

3.why: P3: ledge with 2-bolt anchor after bulges; direction 'left' not confirmed by both, removed.
3.text: Stance is a ledge reached over the two small bulges, anchored on two bolts.

4.why: Sources conflict on P4: one gives a good ledge with 2 bolts, the other a big ledge belay with no bolts mentioned; drop.
